title: Unbounded In-Memory Cache (Missing Cache Eviction)
pattern: Declaring an in-memory collection (such as `HashMap` or `BTreeMap`) acting as a cache that is written to without any associated capacity limit, expiration TTL, or eviction logic (such as LRU or TinyLFU).
why_bad: Memory is a finite resource. A cache without maximum memory limits or an eviction policy will continuously grow as unique keys accumulate, eventually exhausting available RAM and causing OOM crashes [218, 233]. In-memory caches must be tightly bounded or rely on garbage-collector-friendly/SoftReference equivalents to avoid stability-killing degradation [218, 235].
detection: Identify fields in long-lived structs that act as caches but lack size bounds, LRU algorithms, or periodic flush mechanisms.
fix: Wrap the collection in a bounded cache structure (e.g., using `LruCache` or an eviction policy with a configured max size) [219, 233].
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, Chapter 10 (Use Caching Carefully) / passages [218, 219, 233]; Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 4 (Buffer Management) / passage [44].
